text: {"label": "Auditory Stimulus Control and Discrimination","definition": "Research on how sounds and spoken stimuli come to control behavior, including listener and auditory–visual discriminations, auditory equivalence classes, echoics, auditory feedback, hearing voices, and noise-related problem behavior.","distinct_from_neighbours": "Centers on the auditory modality, unlike general stimulus control or equivalence-class formation, and on hearing and discriminating sounds rather than reducing vocal stereotypy or stuttering."}
